purpose: Test noise-aware final selection (NFS): does re-measuring screened configurations on fresh prompts before choosing a few deployable ones beat choosing them from the search archive directly? Designed after C3 (whose extremes-first lock rule did not target the scored region); fixed before any calibration2 or test3 image exists.

splits.calibration2: data/prompts/calibration2.json: 96 COCO prompts (32/32/32), selection seed 20261117, image seed 707, disjoint from calibration, holdout, validation, test, test2
splits.test3: data/prompts/test3.json: 500 COCO prompts (166/167/167), selection seed 20261118, image seed 909, disjoint from all of the above and calibration2

box: objectives (-CLIP, -fidelity, p50 latency, U-Net MB); reference point CLIP = reference CLIP - 1.0, fidelity 75, latency 1.18 x reference latency (median of the job's references; pooled median of job references on calibration), 1,700 MB
stage_a_screen: per arm: pool all candidates as scripts/lock_nas_finalists.py (latency normalized by job reference, signatures merged, CLIP >= ref - 1, fidelity >= 75, black <= ref + 2), 4-objective front, in-box points, greedy hypervolume subset selection of 16 (scripts/c4_screen.py)
naive_control: per arm: the first 5 of the stage-A greedy order, i.e. greedy hypervolume subset selection of 5 on the archive's own calibration measurements
stage_b_remeasure: all screened configurations (shared signatures once) on calibration2, 96 prompts x seed 707, 10 warm-ups, one allocation, 20-step DDIM reference at start, middle and end in a seeded shuffled order; CLIP and fidelity to ref_a of that job
stage_c_select: per arm: from its 16 screened configurations, eligible if black(calibration) + black(calibration2) <= reference black(calibration, pooled median) + reference black(calibration2) + 2; greedy hypervolume subset selection of 5 using the calibration2 measurements only (box from that job's references). If fewer than 5 are in the box, only those are selected (scripts/c4_select.py)
test: union of all NFS and naive sets (shared signatures run once) plus the reference at start, middle and end, on test3 (500 prompts x seed 909), 10 warm-ups, one allocation, seeded shuffled order; CLIP, fidelity to ref_a, latency, U-Net MB; GFLOPs, peak VRAM, black images, KID/FID vs real COCO as secondary
indicator: 4-D hypervolume of a set on test3 inside the box (reference CLIP and latency from the test3 job)
primary_family: NFS vs naive within each arm (4 comparisons): paired prompt bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 0) of HV(NFS) - HV(naive); two-sided bootstrap p; Holm over the 4. NFS is claimed better for an arm if Holm p < 0.05 and the median bootstrap difference is positive. Expectation stated in advance: may be underpowered; when the two sets coincide the difference is 0 and p = 1.
secondary_family: SA-LHFiD+NFS vs each other arm+NFS (3 comparisons), same bootstrap, Holm over the 3, same claim rule. Expectation stated in advance from the post hoc C3 cross-fit: better than random, about level with NSGA-II and SA-NSGA-II.
descriptive: per configuration CLIP non-inferiority vs reference (margin 0.5), fidelity, black images (flag: the 96-image black screen was weak in C3), latency ratio, GFLOPs, peak VRAM, KID/FID; HV of the C3 locks is not part of C4
results_policy: results go to artifacts/analysis/c4*.json and are not written into report, papers or report page without the user's permission
